249	# Settings
250	
251	Frame Job keeps the things that belong to you, not to a project, in one
252	window: how an MCP client reaches the app, your Anthropic key and the
253	assistant's model, your AssemblyAI key and region for cloud transcription,
254	and whether graphics render in the background while you are idle. This page
255	covers every control in that window, the View-menu choices Frame Job
256	remembers between launches, and where the app keeps its files on disk.
257	
258	## Opening Settings
259	
260	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,). It works with or without a project
261	open, so you can set keys from the Welcome window before you make anything.
262	The Assistant tab also opens it for you: when no Anthropic key is set, it
263	shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an
264	**Open Settings…** button. The Generate Captions sheet only tells you where
265	to go: with AssemblyAI chosen and no key set, the note under its button reads
266	"No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸
267	Transcription.", and **Generate** shows the same sentence when you rest the
268	pointer on it.
269	
270	### What each key turns on
271	
272	Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language model or a cloud
273	model needs your own key for it, and without the key the command is greyed
274	rather than hidden:
275	
276	- **Your AssemblyAI key** (Transcription, below) turns on the AssemblyAI
277	  engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and the **Transcribe** buttons of
278	  **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. With no key, **Generate** is greyed when
279	  the AssemblyAI engine is chosen (unless every file is already transcribed,
280	  see [Captions](captions.md)), each **Transcribe** button is greyed, and
281	  **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** itself is greyed and reads **Remove Filler
282	  Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)** — unless a file in the project already
283	  has a transcript made with filler words, which it keeps using without a
284	  key.
285	- **Your Anthropic key** (Assistant, below) turns on the assistant. With no
286	  key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the Assistant tab, which says how to
287	  add the key.
288	
289	Resting the pointer on a greyed control shows "No AssemblyAI API key is set.
290	Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." (or the same sentence for
291	Anthropic and **Assistant**). Saving the key turns the commands on at once,
292	even with the sheet still open; there is nothing to relaunch. Everything that
293	runs on your Mac — on-device captions, Remove Silences, Enhance Voice and the
294	rest — needs no key.
295	
296	Settings is one window, not a set of tabs. It holds four sections, top to
297	bottom: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. On a
298	short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls. Closing it
299	loses nothing: every control saves as you use it, or when you press its
300	**Save** button, as described below. While it is open it is listed in the
301	**Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.
302	
303	The Assistant, Transcription and Playback headings each carry an ⓘ button.
304	Rest the pointer on it for a moment to see that section's explanation; click
305	it to keep the explanation open, and click it again (or anywhere else, or
306	press Escape) to close it.
307	
308	*Agents:* no MCP tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Keys, the model,
309	the region and Background render are set only by a person in this window.
310	An agent's cloud tools (`transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine,
311	`transcribe_for_fillers`) do use the key and region saved here, so a person
312	must set the key first; without one they refuse, at the point they would
313	send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸
314	Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use is answered
315	without a key. The assistant's own tool, `assistant_send` (a dev tool), refuses
316	the same way with the Anthropic sentence.
317	
318	## MCP
319	
320	This section tells an MCP client, such as Claude Code, how to reach
321	Frame Job. Its text is shown in full rather than behind an ⓘ:
322	
323	> An MCP client such as Claude Code uses Frame Job's tools through
324	> framejob-mcp, a helper inside this app. It reaches Frame Job over a local
325	> socket that only programs you run can open.
326	>
327	> If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the
328	> background. To add Frame Job to Claude Code, copy the command and run it in
329	> Terminal.
330	
331	Under the text is the full path of the `framejob-mcp` helper inside the copy
332	of Frame Job you are running. You can select and copy it.
333	
334	**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code
335	on the clipboard, with that path filled in and quoted for the shell:
336	
337	```sh
338	claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
339	```
340	
341	After a copy the section says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press
342	Return." The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so
343	if you move Frame Job, copy the command again.
344	
345	If the helper is missing from this copy of the app, the button is disabled
346	and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."
347	
348	Other clients, the socket and the tool list are covered in [MCP](mcp.md).
349	
350	## Assistant
351	
352	This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic API key, the
353	model, and two settings for long conversations. The assistant itself is
354	described in [Assistant](assistant.md).
355	
356	| Control | What it does | Default |
357	|---|---|---|
358	| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or Return. | None |
359	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | — |
360	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Disabled when no key is stored. | — |
361	| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses. Saved when you press Return or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
362	| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000. | On, 300,000 |
363	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn (never tool search results). | Off |
364	
365	### The key
366	
367	Your key is never shown again once saved. When a key is stored, the field
368	shows a fixed row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same
369	length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in
370	the field. When no key is stored, the field reads "Paste your key". The line
371	under the controls says "Key saved." or "Key removed." after a press. It says
372	"No API key is set." (in ordinary grey, not as an error) whenever there is no
373	key in the field, the store or the environment.
374	
375	If the key file cannot be written (for example, because its folder is not
376	writable), the field is still emptied and the line reads "The API key could
377	not be saved: <reason>", styled as a problem. A Remove that fails shows the
378	same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays.
379	
380	There is no Verify button here. The app does not call Anthropic itself; the
381	key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.
382	
383	### What a change does
384	
385	- **Saving or removing the key, or changing the model**, ends the
386	  conversation in every open window's Assistant tab. A conversation keeps the
387	  key and model it started with, so the next message starts a new one.
388	  Pressing Return in the Model field without changing what it resolves to
389	  ends nothing.
390	- **Changing the compaction or clearing settings** takes effect in every open
391	  conversation at once and keeps each one going. There is no Save button for
392	  these. A threshold outside 20,000–900,000 beeps and the field goes back to
393	  the stored number.
394	
395	Compaction happens at the end of a turn, and renders from earlier in the
396	conversation do not survive it. Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache
397	write.
398	
399	### What the ⓘ says
400	
401	The Assistant ⓘ sums up what the assistant sends and where:
402	
403	- it sends your messages, the project's details and the frames it renders to
404	  Anthropic, using your own API key, and what it costs is billed to that key;
405	- it asks before writing a file;
406	- the key is kept in a file only you can read and is never shown again once
407	  saved;
408	- a blank Model means `claude-opus-5-5`, and changing the key or the model
409	  starts a new conversation;
410	- the compaction and clearing settings, as in the table above.
411	
412	### This month's spend
413	
414	Under the buttons is what the assistant has cost in the current calendar
415	month, in UTC, for example "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 37 responses." It
416	is read from the spend ledger (see [Where Frame Job keeps its
417	files](#where-frame-job-keeps-its-files)) each time Settings opens, and
418	again after every response while the window is open. Other forms it can take:
419	
420	- "Nothing recorded in October 2026 (UTC)." for a month with no responses;
421	- "…; none could be priced." or "…; 3 could not be priced, the rest came to
422	  $0.80." when some responses had no price (they are counted, never added as
423	  $0);
424	- a positive amount that would round to $0.00 (less than half a cent)
425	  reads "under $0.01";
426	- " 2 ledger lines could not be read." is added to the sentence when some
427	  lines of the ledger are damaged;
428	- "Reading the spend ledger…" while it is being read, and "The spend ledger
429	  could not be read: …" if it cannot be;
430	- "This launch keeps no spend ledger." when Frame Job has no folder to keep
431	  one in.
432	
433	The note beneath says what the figure is: "Frame Job's own estimate at
434	LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your
435	account was billed." The Assistant tab's own Spend row, for the current
436	conversation, is described in [Assistant](assistant.md).
437	
438	## Transcription
439	
440	This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. They are used when you
441	choose AssemblyAI in **File ▸ Generate Captions…** (see
442	[Captions](captions.md)) and by **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**, which
443	finds fillers only through AssemblyAI (see [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md)).
444	On-device captions need no key.
445	
446	| Control | What it does | Default |
447	|---|---|---|
448	| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or Return. | None |
449	| **Region:** | Which AssemblyAI data region to use: **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
450	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | — |
451	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Disabled when no key is stored. | — |
452	| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request with the key and region, to check the key works. | — |
453	| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard (assemblyai.com/dashboard) in your browser, where you get a key and see what you have spent. | — |
454	
455	The key field behaves exactly like the Assistant's: a fixed row of dots when
456	a key is stored, "Paste your key" when one is not, and "Key saved.",
457	"Key removed." or "No API key is set." on the line beneath, and "The API key
458	could not be saved: <reason>" if the key file cannot be written or removed.
459	
460	A transcript made in one region cannot be seen from the other, so the region
461	is a choice you make, not a fallback. Pick the region your AssemblyAI account
462	uses.
463	
464	### Verify
465	
466	**Verify** checks whichever key a real run would use: the one typed in the
467	field if you have typed one and not saved it yet, otherwise the stored key,
468	otherwise the key in the environment (see below). It is disabled when there
469	is no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running.
470	
471	| Line under the controls | Meaning |
472	|---|---|
473	| Checking… | The request is in flight. |
474	| Key accepted | AssemblyAI accepted the key in this region. |
475	| Settings changed since this check began. Verify again. | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
476	| An AssemblyAI message, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The check failed; the text says why. |
477	
478	Saving, removing or changing the region also tells an open Generate Captions
479	sheet straight away, so it can enable its button without being reopened.
480	
481	### What the ⓘ says
482	
483	The Transcription ⓘ explains what leaves your Mac: with AssemblyAI chosen,
484	the audio of the files you are captioning is uploaded, transcribed, read back
485	and then deleted from AssemblyAI. Frame Job asks for the delete as soon as it
486	has the words, and retries it at the start of the next run if it did not go
487	through. Nothing is uploaded until you press Generate, and captions made on
488	your Mac never leave it. It also gives AssemblyAI's published rate as Frame
489	Job last read it: $0.21 an hour of audio, $0.02 more with Speakers on (read on
490	2026-09-17).
491	
492	A retried delete is sent with the key and region set at that later run, so
493	it can only succeed with a key for the account and region that made the
494	upload; keep that in mind before changing either. With no key set, the
495	cleanup is deferred and the run reports it. If a transcript could not be
496	saved in the project, Frame Job cannot retry its delete at all, and says so:
497	delete it yourself in AssemblyAI's dashboard (the **Account Page** button).
498	
499	## Playback
500	
501	This section has one row: whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time
502	while you are idle, and how long it waits first.
503	
504	| Control | What it does | Default |
505	|---|---|---|
506	| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last, so they play smoothly from the start. | On |
507	| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle before it starts. Type a whole number from 1 to 60, or use the stepper. Disabled while Background render is off. | 5 |
508	
509	Both save the moment you change them. A number outside 1–60 beeps and the
510	field goes back to the stored value.
511	
512	Anything you do in Frame Job (a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a
513	seek) stops the pass at once, and the wait starts again from zero. An agent's
514	calls over MCP count too when they edit a project or move a playhead; a call
515	that only reads, such as `get_project`, does not. Moving the
516	pointer alone does not count, and neither does what you do in other apps. It
517	never runs while a window is playing. While it runs it keeps the processor
518	busy. The frames it draws are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's
519	memory and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames
520	replace them. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
521	
522	## Updates
523	
524	The copy of Frame Job you download from the project's GitHub Releases page
525	updates itself, with [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). A copy you build
526	from source (`make app`, `make app-debug`) has no updater: no menu item, and
527	it never checks.
528	
529	- **Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…**, directly under About Frame Job, checks
530	  now. When a newer Frame Job has been published, a window shows its version
531	  and a link to its release page, and offers to install it; **Install
532	  Update** replaces the app and relaunches it. When there is nothing newer,
533	  it says you are up to date. The item is greyed out while a check is
534	  already running.
535	- **Automatic checks.** The second time you open Frame Job, it asks whether
536	  to check for updates automatically. If you agree, it checks about once a
537	  day while it is open, and tells you when an update is ready; it never
538	  installs one without asking you.
539	
540	Every update is signed, and Frame Job refuses one whose signature does not
541	match the key built into the app, so only a release published from the
542	project itself can be installed. Updates are always the whole app; release
543	notes are on the release's page on GitHub.
544	
545	There is no Settings control for automatic checks. Your answer is kept in
546	macOS's preferences for Frame Job (below); to turn checks off later, run
547	`defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool NO` in
548	Terminal while Frame Job is closed, and **Check for Updates…** still works.
549	
550	*Agents:* no MCP tool checks for or installs updates.
551	
552	## View settings Frame Job remembers
553	
554	These are View-menu choices, not Settings controls, but Frame Job remembers
555	them between launches: the last choice you made, in any window, is what the
556	next window opens with.
557	
558	| Setting | Where | Choices | Default |
559	|---|---|---|---|
560	| Snapping | **View ▸ Snapping**, the bare key N, or the timeline bar's **Snap** toggle | On / off (a checkmark) | On |
561	| Safe area guides | **View ▸ Safe Areas**, or the **Safe** checkbox in the preview toolbar | On / off | Off |
562	| Inspector | **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (⌥⌘I); reads **Show Inspector** while hidden | Shown / hidden | Shown |
563	| Timeline track height | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸**, or the timeline bar's S / M / L buttons (Small tracks, Medium tracks, Large tracks) | Small · Medium · Large | Medium |
564	| Preview quality | **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸** | Full · Half · Quarter | Full |
565	| Pane sizes | Drag the dividers | Inspector width 280–440 pt; timeline height from 140 pt to 60% of the window | Inspector 304 pt, timeline 300 pt |
566	
567	Only dragging a divider saves a pane size. Resizing the window, or hiding and
568	showing the inspector, changes nothing remembered, and the inspector's width
569	is not saved while it is hidden.
570	
571	Preview Quality changes only how sharply the preview is drawn while you
572	work. Export and saved frames always render at full size. Holding ⌘ while
573	you drag turns snapping off for that drag only, and changes nothing that is
574	remembered. See [Timeline](timeline.md) and [Canvas and
575	layers](canvas-and-layers.md).
576	
577	Other View items, such as **Preview Window**, **Show Ungraded**, **Show
578	Selection**, **Show SDR Version** and **Scopes**, are not remembered; they
579	start off in each new window. The preview window's position and size are
580	remembered, though: there is one saved frame for every project, so a preview
581	opens where the last one was left, on a second display for example. With two
582	projects' previews open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and
583	only one of them saves where it is moved. A full list is in [Menus and
584	shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md).
585	
586	## Other choices Frame Job remembers
587	
588	Some sheets and panels reopen on what you chose last time. These are your
589	choices, not the project's, and no agent tool reads them.
590	
591	| What | Remembered | Page |
592	|---|---|---|
593	| **File ▸ Generate Captions…** | The engine (On this Mac or AssemblyAI), the Style, and the Slide the pill, Fill words as spoken and Dim in pauses boxes | [Captions](captions.md) |
594	| **File ▸ Export…** | The last settings you exported with; named presets are kept in a file (below) | [Export](export.md) |
595	| Document tab | **Resize clips proportionally**, used with the next canvas-size change | [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md#canvas) |
596	| Recorder panel | Display, microphone, System Audio, show clicks, frame rate, size and **Include Frame Job windows** | [Screen recording](screen-recording.md) |
597	| Inspector sections | Whether each section is collapsed or expanded, per section, in every window. A section you have never clicked opens in its default state (Transform, a text or shape's main section and a graphic's Properties open, the rest closed). | [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md) |
598	| Screen Recording permission | That Frame Job has already asked macOS once. macOS will not show its prompt twice, so later presses of Record without the permission open System Settings' Screen Recording pane instead. | [Screen recording](screen-recording.md) |

602	All of these, and the View settings above, live in macOS's preferences for
603	Frame Job (the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain). Keys are never stored

606	## Where Frame Job keeps its files
607	
608	Frame Job's own folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. It is
609	created only when something first needs it, at a mode only you can open; if
610	you have already set the folder's permissions yourself, Frame Job leaves them
611	alone.
612	
613	| Path | What it is |
614	|---|---|
615	| `…/Frame Job/assemblyai-key` | Your AssemblyAI key. |
616	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-key` | Your Anthropic key. |
617	| `…/Frame Job/spend.jsonl` | The spend ledger: one line per assistant response, with its time, model, token counts and estimated dollars. It never holds your key or the conversation. |
618	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json` | The assistant's cached copy of the price table it uses for that estimate. |
619	| `…/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json` | Your named export presets. |
620	| `…/Frame Job/Rewrapped/` | Movies Frame Job converted or repackaged from files macOS could not open. A project refers to these files; moving them leaves the media missing until you relink. |
621	| `…/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock` | The local socket MCP clients connect to, created at every launch. |
622	| `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` | Screen recordings and voice-overs, named by date and time (for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`; a voice-over is `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`). |
623	
624	Projects themselves are `.framejob` packages wherever you save them, and hold
625	their own caches (see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).
626	
627	### How keys are stored
628	
629	Each key is a plain file, readable and writable only by your user account
630	(mode `0600`). It is written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so
631	it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written. Keys are
632	never put in macOS preferences, never logged, never passed as a launch
633	argument and never shown in the window again. Frame Job does not use the
634	Keychain. Anything running as your user account can read these files, so
635	treat your Mac account as the protection.
636	
637	### Keys from the environment
638	
639	If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable, which
640	is useful when you launch it from a terminal:
641	
642	| Key | Variable |
643	|---|---|
644	| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
645	| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |
646	
647	A stored key always wins over the variable. An empty variable counts as no
648	key. **Verify** checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or stored.
649	
650	## Limits
651	
652	- Settings has no MCP mirror. An agent cannot set or read a key, the model,
653	  the region or Background render.
654	- There is no button to forget the remembered convert-on-import answer. To
655	  be asked again, run `defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport`
656	  in Terminal while Frame Job is closed.
657	- Converting on import needs `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. Frame Job looks for them
658	  on `PATH` and in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`,
659	  `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. For an install elsewhere, run
660	  `defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg`;
661	  `ffprobe` is taken from beside it, or else found by the same search.
662	- An unknown or missing region reads as United States.
663	- The MCP command copied is for Claude Code. Other MCP clients use the same
664	  helper path in their own configuration; see [MCP](mcp.md).

294	/// Settings' Verify button and its bookkeeping: which key and region a check
295	/// ran against, the transcriber it holds while it runs, and whether its
296	/// answer still describes what the window shows. A pure move out of
297	/// `SettingsWindowController.swift` (#58); the stored `verifying` stays there,
298	/// because an extension cannot store.
299	extension SettingsWindowController {
300	    struct VerificationInput: Equatable {
301	        let credential: String
302	        let region: AssemblyAIConfiguration.Region
303	        let base: URL
304	    }
305	
306	    struct Verification {
307	        let id: UUID
308	        let input: VerificationInput
309	        let transcriber: CloudTranscriber
310	    }
311	
312	    func effectiveCredential(storedCredential: String?) -> String? {
313	        let typed = keyField.stringValue.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
314	        if !typed.isEmpty { return typed }
315	        if let storedCredential { return storedCredential }
316	        guard let value = environment[AssemblyAIConfiguration.environmentKey] else { return nil }
317	        let trimmed = value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
318	        return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed
319	    }
320	
321	    func verificationInput(credential: String) throws -> VerificationInput {
322	        VerificationInput(
323	            credential: credential,
324	            region: AssemblyAIConfiguration.region(defaults: defaults),
325	            base: try AssemblyAIConfiguration.baseURL(defaults: defaults))
326	    }
327	
328	    func updateVerifyButton(credential: String?) {
329	        guard let credential else {
330	            verifyButton?.isEnabled = false
331	            return
332	        }
333	        if let verifying,
334	            (try? verificationInput(credential: credential)) == verifying.input
335	        {
336	            verifyButton?.isEnabled = false
337	        } else {
338	            verifyButton?.isEnabled = true
339	        }
340	    }
341	
342	    /// The cheapest authenticated call there is, against whatever key would
343	    /// be used for a real run: what is in the FIELD when somebody has typed
344	    /// one and not saved it yet, and the resolved credential otherwise.
345	    @objc func verifyClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
346	        verifying = nil
347	        guard let credential = effectiveCredential(storedCredential: store().read()) else {
348	            updateVerifyButton(credential: nil)
349	            say("No API key is set.", problem: false)
350	            return
351	        }
352	        let input: VerificationInput
353	        do {
354	            input = try verificationInput(credential: credential)
355	        } catch {
356	            updateVerifyButton(credential: credential)
357	            say(error.localizedDescription, problem: true)
358	            return
359	        }
360	        say("Checking…", problem: false)
361	        verifyButton.isEnabled = false
362	        // The cache directory and the media list are what a RUN needs and a
363	        // verify never touches; the temporary folder is the honest "nowhere".
364	        let transcriber = CloudTranscriber(
365	            client: AssemblyAIClient(base: input.base, credential: input.credential),
366	            cacheDirectory: URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory(), isDirectory: true),
367	            media: [:])
368	        let id = UUID()
369	        verifying = Verification(id: id, input: input, transcriber: transcriber)
370	        transcriber.verify { [weak self] answer in
371	            self?.completeVerification(answer, id: id, input: input)
372	        }
373	    }
374	
375	    private func completeVerification(
376	        _ answer: Result<Void, AssemblyAIClient.ClientError>,
377	        id: UUID, input: VerificationInput
378	    ) {
379	        guard verifying?.id == id else { return }
380	        verifying = nil
381	        let credential = effectiveCredential(storedCredential: store().read())
382	        updateVerifyButton(credential: credential)
383	        guard let credential,
384	            (try? verificationInput(credential: credential)) == input
385	        else {
386	            say("Settings changed since this check began. Verify again.", problem: false)
387	            return
388	        }
389	        switch answer {
390	        case .success:
391	            say("Key accepted", problem: false)
392	        case .failure(let error):
393	            say(error.localizedDescription, problem: true)
394	        }
395	    }

571	/// Settings' MCP pane (issue batch B74, spec §11 MC-7): the first of
572	/// `SettingsWindowController`'s panes. It says how an MCP client reaches
573	/// Frame Job — through the bundled `framejob-mcp` (MC-1, MC-3), which opens
574	/// Frame Job in the background on the first tool call (MC-4) — shows that
575	/// helper's path, and holds Copy MCP Command, which puts MC-3's line on the
576	/// pasteboard.
577	///
578	/// **The blurb is visible, not behind an ⓘ** (MC-7): the owner asked for it
579	/// above the button, so the heading has no `SettingsInfoButton`.
580	///
581	/// **One spelling of the path and the line.** The helper's URL arrives from
582	/// `AgentServer.mcpHelperURL` through `SettingsWindowController`'s defaulted
583	/// parameter, and the line is `AgentServer.mcpCommand(helperPath:)`; the pane
584	/// builds neither itself. The pasteboard is a parameter too, so a probe hands
585	/// it a private one and never writes the general pasteboard.
586	///
587	/// **The button is enabled exactly while the helper is executable.** A copy
588	/// of Frame Job without it says so in the status line. The press is not an
589	/// edit, so it has no MCP mirror (spec §7.9).
590	final class MCPSettingsPane: NSStackView {
591	    static let paneTitle = "MCP"
592	    static let blurb = [
593	        "An MCP client such as Claude Code uses Frame Job's tools through framejob-mcp, a helper "
594	            + "inside this app. It reaches Frame Job over a local socket that only programs you "
595	            + "run can open.",
596	        "If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background. To add "
597	            + "Frame Job to Claude Code, copy the command and run it in Terminal.",
598	    ]
599	    static let copyTitle = "Copy MCP Command"
600	    static let copiedStatus = "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."
601	    static let missingStatus = "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."
602	    /// The Settings window's width less its two insets.
603	    private static let textWidth: CGFloat = 420
604	
605	    let helperURL: URL
606	    let pasteboard: NSPasteboard
607	
608	    let headingLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: MCPSettingsPane.paneTitle)
609	    let blurbLabels: [NSTextField] = MCPSettingsPane.blurb.map {
610	        NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: $0)
611	    }
612	    let helperLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
613	    let statusLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
614	    private(set) var copyButton: NSButton!
615	
616	    /// MC-3's line for this pane's helper.
617	    var command: String { AgentServer.mcpCommand(helperPath: helperURL.path) }
618	
619	    init(helperURL: URL, pasteboard: NSPasteboard) {
620	        self.helperURL = helperURL
621	        self.pasteboard = pasteboard
622	        super.init(frame: .zero)
623	        build()
624	        sync()
625	    }
626	
627	    @available(*, unavailable)
628	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
629	        fatalError("MCPSettingsPane does not support NSCoder")
630	    }
631	
632	    private func build() {
633	        headingLabel.font = DS.sans(15, weight: .bold)
634	        headingLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
635	        headingLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.mcp.heading")
636	
637	        for (index, label) in blurbLabels.enumerated() {
638	            label.font = DS.sans(13)
639	            label.textColor = DS.textStrong
640	            label.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = Self.textWidth
641	            label.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.mcp.blurb.\(index + 1)")
642	        }
643	
644	        helperLabel.stringValue = helperURL.path
645	        helperLabel.font = DS.mono(12)
646	        helperLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
647	        helperLabel.isSelectable = true
648	        helperLabel.lineBreakMode = .byCharWrapping
649	        helperLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = Self.textWidth
650	        helperLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.mcp.helper")
651	
652	        statusLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
653	        statusLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
654	        statusLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = Self.textWidth
655	        statusLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.mcp.status")
656	
657	        copyButton = StickerButton(
658	            title: Self.copyTitle, style: .secondary, target: self,
659	            action: #selector(copyClicked(_:)))
660	        copyButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.mcp.copy")
661	
662	        orientation = .vertical
663	        alignment = .leading
664	        spacing = 12
665	        let views: [NSView] = [headingLabel] + blurbLabels + [helperLabel, copyButton, statusLabel]
666	        for view in views { addArrangedSubview(view) }
667	        for label in blurbLabels.dropLast() { setCustomSpacing(8, after: label) }
668	    }
669	
670	    /// Whether the button can do anything, and the status that goes with it:
671	    /// empty while the helper is executable, `missingStatus` while it is not.
672	    func sync() {
673	        let present = FileManager.default.isExecutableFile(atPath: helperURL.path)
674	        copyButton.isEnabled = present
675	        statusLabel.stringValue = present ? "" : Self.missingStatus
676	    }
677	
678	    /// Puts MC-3's line on the pane's pasteboard. A helper that went missing
679	    /// since the last sync writes nothing and shows why.
680	    @objc func copyClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
681	        guard FileManager.default.isExecutableFile(atPath: helperURL.path) else {
682	            sync()
683	            return
684	        }
685	        pasteboard.clearContents()
686	        pasteboard.setString(command, forType: .string)
687	        statusLabel.stringValue = Self.copiedStatus
688	    }
689	}

692	/// Settings' Playback pane (spec §11 G-38 (a)): Background render, on, and
693	/// the idle wait before it starts, under the Transcription pane in
694	/// `SettingsWindowController`'s one stack. Its heading carries a
695	/// `SettingsInfoButton` holding `explanation()` (SH-5).
696	///
697	/// One row, AssistantSettingsPane's compaction row's shape: the checkbox,
698	/// "Start after", the seconds field and its stepper, "seconds". The field and
699	/// the stepper are enabled only while the box is ticked. Each control saves
700	/// at once through `BackgroundRenderSettings.save`, with no Save button; a
701	/// field value outside `delayRange` beeps and shows the stored value again,
702	/// writing nothing. The pane holds no reference to `BackgroundRender`: a
703	/// click or a key in it is activity like any other, and every restart of
704	/// the idle clock reads the stored delay. It is a person's setting — no tool
705	/// reads or writes it (AI-11, R6-12).
706	final class PlaybackSettingsPane: NSStackView {
707	    static let paneTitle = "Playback"
708	    static let backgroundTitle = "Background render"
709	    static let delayText = "Start after"
710	    static let secondsText = "seconds"
711	
712	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
713	
714	    let headingLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: PlaybackSettingsPane.paneTitle)
715	    /// The heading's ⓘ, holding `explanation()` (SH-5).
716	    let infoButton = SettingsInfoButton(
717	        section: PlaybackSettingsPane.paneTitle, infoText: PlaybackSettingsPane.explanation())
718	    let backgroundBox = NSButton(
719	        checkboxWithTitle: PlaybackSettingsPane.backgroundTitle, target: nil, action: nil)
720	    let delayField = NSTextField()
721	    let delayStepper = NSStepper()
722	    let secondsLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: PlaybackSettingsPane.secondsText)
723	
724	    init(defaults: UserDefaults) {
725	        self.defaults = defaults
726	        super.init(frame: .zero)
727	        build()
728	        sync()
729	    }
730	
731	    @available(*, unavailable)
732	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
733	        fatalError("PlaybackSettingsPane does not support NSCoder")
734	    }
735	
736	    private func build() {
737	        headingLabel.font = DS.sans(15, weight: .bold)
738	        headingLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
739	        headingLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.playback.heading")
740	        infoButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.playback.info")
741	
742	        backgroundBox.font = DS.sans(13)
743	        backgroundBox.target = self
744	        backgroundBox.action = #selector(backgroundToggled(_:))
745	        backgroundBox.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.playback.background")
746	
747	        let delayLabel = fieldLabel(Self.delayText)
748	        DSField.style(delayField)
749	        delayField.alignment = .right
750	        delayField.target = self
751	        delayField.action = #selector(delayChanged(_:))
752	        delayField.cell?.sendsActionOnEndEditing = true
753	        delayField.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 44).isActive = true
754	        delayField.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.playback.delay")
755	
756	        let range = BackgroundRenderSettings.delayRange
757	        delayStepper.minValue = Double(range.lowerBound)
758	        delayStepper.maxValue = Double(range.upperBound)
759	        delayStepper.increment = 1
760	        delayStepper.valueWraps = false
761	        delayStepper.autorepeat = true
762	        delayStepper.target = self
763	        delayStepper.action = #selector(delayStepped(_:))
764	        delayStepper.setAccessibilityIdentifier("settings.playback.stepper")
765	
766	        secondsLabel.font = DS.sans(13)
767	        secondsLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
768	
769	        orientation = .vertical
770	        alignment = .leading
771	        spacing = 12
772	        let delayRow = NSStackView(
773	            views: [backgroundBox, delayLabel, delayField, delayStepper, secondsLabel])
774	        delayRow.orientation = .horizontal
775	        delayRow.alignment = .centerY
776	        delayRow.spacing = 6
777	        // Hugs at its content, so its width is not a tie with the column's (#143).
778	        delayRow.setHuggingPriority(.required, for: .horizontal)
779	        addArrangedSubview(settingsSectionHeader(headingLabel, info: infoButton))
780	        addArrangedSubview(delayRow)
781	    }

783	    // MARK: - Syncing
784	
785	    /// The stored setting on the controls; the field and the stepper enabled
786	    /// only while the box is ticked, the field never written while it is
787	    /// being edited. Reads only, never writes.
788	    func sync() {
789	        let settings = BackgroundRenderSettings.load(from: defaults)
790	        backgroundBox.state = settings.enabled ? .on : .off
791	        delayField.isEnabled = settings.enabled
792	        delayStepper.isEnabled = settings.enabled
793	        delayStepper.integerValue = settings.delaySeconds
794	        if delayField.currentEditor() == nil {
795	            delayField.stringValue = String(settings.delaySeconds)
796	        }
797	    }
798	
799	    // MARK: - Controls
800	
801	    @objc func backgroundToggled(_ sender: Any?) {
802	        var settings = BackgroundRenderSettings.load(from: defaults)
803	        settings.enabled = backgroundBox.state == .on
804	        settings.save(to: defaults)
805	        sync()
806	    }
807	
808	    /// The field's commit (Return or leaving it). Outside the range beeps and
809	    /// shows the stored value again, writing nothing.
810	    @objc func delayChanged(_ sender: Any?) {
811	        var settings = BackgroundRenderSettings.load(from: defaults)
812	        let typed = delayField.stringValue.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
813	        guard let seconds = Int(typed), BackgroundRenderSettings.delayRange.contains(seconds) else {
814	            NSSound.beep()
815	            delayField.stringValue = String(settings.delaySeconds)
816	            return
817	        }
818	        settings.delaySeconds = seconds
819	        settings.save(to: defaults)
820	        sync()
821	        delayField.stringValue = String(seconds)
822	    }
823	
824	    @objc func delayStepped(_ sender: Any?) {
825	        var settings = BackgroundRenderSettings.load(from: defaults)
826	        settings.delaySeconds = delayStepper.integerValue
827	        settings.save(to: defaults)
828	        sync()
829	        delayField.stringValue = String(settings.delaySeconds)
830	    }
831	
832	    /// The ⓘ's text in two paragraphs: what the pass does and when, and
833	    /// where its frames are held.
834	    static func explanation() -> String {
835	        [
836	            "While you leave Frame Job alone for the time set here, it draws the graphics "
837	                + "after the playhead in the window you last used, so they play smoothly from the "
838	                + "start. It stops as soon as you do anything in Frame Job and starts again after "
839	                + "the same wait, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs.",
840	            "The frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of this Mac's and less when memory "
841	                + "is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them.",
842	        ].joined(separator: "\n\n")
843	    }

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```

sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order

Tick **Do this automatically from now on** in the alert to keep the answer you give:

There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:

defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
```

That setting holds `ask`, `always` or `never`, and `ask` is the default.

Click **Loop**, the repeat button at the end of the transport in the toolbar. The button is dimmed while Loop is off and full strength while it's on. Click it again to turn Loop off.

---
title: "Buttons and context menus"
description: "Every toolbar and timeline-bar button with no menu item, and every right-click menu in Frame Job, with what each item does and when it's greyed."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most commands live in the menu bar, and [Menus](/reference/menus/) lists them. This page covers the rest: the buttons that do something no menu item does, and the menus you open with a right-click.

<AtAGlance
  keys="⌃-click"
  where={['The toolbar', 'The timeline bar', 'Right-click a track, a Media row, an inspector row or a curves channel']}
  tools={['add_shape_clip', 'set_track', 'remove_track', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_action_end', 'set_video', 'record_screen']}
/>

## Buttons with no menu item

Most buttons in the toolbar and the timeline bar repeat a menu item, and their tooltips give its shortcut. These four have no menu item at all.

| Button | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Loop** | Toolbar, at the end of the transport buttons | Turns [looping](/timeline/loop/) on and off. Playback repeats the in/out range when one is set, otherwise the whole timeline. The button is dimmed while Loop is off. |
| **Zoom Out** and **Zoom In** (− and +) | Timeline bar | Zoom the [timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) out or in by a step. |
| **Timeline Zoom** slider | Timeline bar, between − and + | Sets the timeline zoom about the middle of the view. The slider is logarithmic, so the same distance always changes the zoom by the same ratio. |
| **Add Shape** | Timeline bar | Opens the shape menu. See [Add Shape](#add-shape). |

These have their own control, and do the same as a **View** menu item:

| Button | Where | The same as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Fit Timeline** | Timeline bar, after + | **View ▸ Fit Timeline** (<kbd>⇧Z</kbd>) |
| **Snap** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Snapping** (<kbd>N</kbd>) |
| **S**, **M** and **L** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**: Small, Medium and Large tracks |
| Zoom pop-up: **Fit**, **50%**, **100%**, **200%** | Toolbar | The canvas zoom. **View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** move through the same four steps. |
| **Safe** | Toolbar | **View ▸ Safe Areas** |

## Add Shape

The **Add Shape** button in the timeline bar is the only way to add a shape clip. There's no menu bar item for it.

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.
2. Click **Add Shape**.
3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.

</Steps>

The shape goes on the front track at the playhead. If it doesn't fit there, Frame Job adds a new track above everything and puts it on that. The new clip is selected, and the undo step names the shape, for example **Add Ellipse**. See [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/).

## Context menus

Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click opens a menu in four places in the editor:

- [A track's header, or the empty part of its lane](#track-header-or-empty-lane)
- [A row in the Media tab](#media-row)
- [A row in the inspector](#inspector-row)
- [A channel in the Color tab's curves strip](#curves-channel-strip)

A right-click on a clip, the ruler or the timeline's corner opens no menu.

A menu acts on what you clicked, not on the selection or the current track.

### Track header or empty lane

Right-click a track's header, one of the buttons on it, or the empty part of its lane. The menu is for that track, and its checkmarks show that track's own state.

| Item | What it does | Undo step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hide Video** | Turns the track's picture off or on. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). | Hide Track |
| **Mute Audio** | Turns the track's sound off or on. | Mute Track |
| **Lock Track** | Locks or unlocks the track. | Lock Track |
| **Solo** | Solos the track, or stops soloing it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). | Solo Track |
| **Mix…** | Opens the track's mix panel. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). | |
| **Matte ▸** | **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**, with a checkmark on the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/). | Track Matte |
| **Remove Track** | Removes the track. If it holds clips, Frame Job asks first and says how many go with it. Greyed when it's the only track. | Remove Track |

**Remove Track** here is the way to delete an empty track that isn't the front-most one, because an empty track has no clip to select.

### Media row

Right-click a row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). The menu acts on that file, whatever the list's selection is.

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, pushing later clips along, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/). |
| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, replacing what's in the way, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. |
| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips that use the file, scrolls to the first one and switches to the Clip tab. Greyed when no clip on the timeline itself uses the file, which includes a file no clip uses and one used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/). |
| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder: the original, or the project's copy when there's no original. It beeps when it has neither. |
| **Relink…** | Points this entry at a file you choose. It takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate and its audio, video and alpha flags. Frame Job won't relink to a file of another kind, and a clip past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/). |
| **Remove** | Removes the file from the project. An unused file goes at once. A used file asks first, and its clips go with it, including clips inside nests. When the file is a LUT, the clips using it keep their place and lose the look, and any file it converts loses its Camera Log. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |

### Inspector row

Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them. The menu shows only what applies to that row, and with nothing that applies there's no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own menu.

| Item | When it's there | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action. |
| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action. |
| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default. Greyed when it's already there. |
| **Set end value to default** | The row has a default and animates, and an action is selected | Takes the place of **Reset to default**, and sets the row's value at the action's end. Greyed when it's already there. |

On a row the selected action changes, the ◆ in the left gutter turns into × when you hover over it. Click it to remove the row from the action, the same as **Remove from action N**. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

### Curves channel strip

Right-click a cell of the channel strip under the curve editor in the Color tab. **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat** puts that one curve back to flat, and is greyed when it already is.

### Recording status item

This one is in the macOS menu bar, not the editor. While a recording runs its time shows there, and a click opens its menu:

- **Recording keyboard shortcuts**, a dimmed row shown only while shortcuts are being recorded
- **Pause Recording**, or **Resume Recording** while paused
- **Stop Recording**

Its tooltip says whether Frame Job is recording or paused. If you quit while a display or window recording is running with the recorder panel hidden, Frame Job opens this menu so you can stop it.

If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **Pause Recording** still work. See [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/).

## Related

- [Menus](/reference/menus/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
- [Gestures with no menu item](/reference/gestures/)

---
title: "Settings"
description: "Every control in the Settings window: connecting an MCP client, your Anthropic and AssemblyAI keys, the assistant's model, and background rendering."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Settings holds what belongs to you and not to a project: how an MCP client reaches Frame Job, your Anthropic key and the assistant's model, your AssemblyAI key and region, and whether graphics render while you're idle.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Assistant tab ▸ Open Settings…"
/>

<Shot
  name="02-settings.window"
  alt="The Assistant, Transcription and Playback sections of Settings with no keys stored. Assistant has an Anthropic API key field reading Paste your key, a Model field, Compact when context reaches 300,000 tokens ticked, Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens unticked, and Save and Remove buttons. Transcription has an AssemblyAI API key field, Region set to United States, and Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page buttons. Playback has Background render ticked, starting after 5 seconds."
/>

## Opening Settings

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). It works with or without a project open, so you can set your keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It's a window, not a sheet, and it shows the same settings whichever project is open.

The window has four sections, one under the other: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. There are no tabs. On a short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls.

Closing it loses nothing, because every control saves as you use it, or when you press its **Save** button. While it's open it's listed in the **Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.

Two other places send you here:

- With no Anthropic key, the Assistant tab shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button that opens this window.
- With AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note under the button in the Generate Captions sheet, and the button's tooltip, read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The sheet doesn't open Settings for you.

[AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/) says what each key turns on.

## The info buttons

The **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback** headings each carry an ⓘ button that explains the section. The MCP section has none, because its text is shown in full.

- Rest the pointer on it for about a third of a second to see the explanation. Moving away closes it.
- Click it to keep the explanation open. Click it again, click anywhere else, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or close the window to end it.

VoiceOver reads it as "About Assistant", and so on for each section. With keyboard navigation on, <kbd>Space</kbd> presses it.

## MCP

This section tells an MCP client, such as Claude Code, how to reach Frame Job. Clients use `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which connects over a local socket that only programs you run can open. If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background.

Under that text is the full path of the helper inside the copy you're running. You can select and copy it.

**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

The section then says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."

The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job. If the helper is missing from this copy, the button is dimmed and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."

The command is for Claude Code. Other clients use the same helper path in their own configuration. See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

## Assistant

This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic key, the model, and two settings for long conversations. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses, typed as text. Saved when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000, and the field works only while the box is ticked. | On, 300,000 |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn. It never drops tool search results. | Off |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |

There's no **Verify** button here, because Frame Job doesn't call Anthropic itself. Your key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.

**A change to the key or the model starts over.** Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window's Assistant tab, and the next message starts a new one. Pressing <kbd>Return</kbd> in **Model:** without changing the model that's used ends nothing.

**A change to the other two keeps going.** The compaction and clearing settings apply to every open conversation at once and end none of them. They have no **Save** button. A compaction number outside 20,000 to 900,000 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Earlier renders don't survive compaction, and each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).

Under the buttons is what the assistant has cost this month, with a note that the figure is Frame Job's own estimate. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).

The ⓘ sums up what's sent to Anthropic, that it's billed to your key, that the assistant asks before writing a file, where the key is kept, the blank **Model:** default and the two chat settings.

## Transcription

This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** uses them with AssemblyAI chosen, and so does **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Captions made on your Mac need no key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with the key and region, to check they work. | |
| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard in your browser, where you get a key and see what you've spent. | |

A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your AssemblyAI account uses.

**Verify** checks the key a real run would use: one you've typed and not saved, otherwise the stored key, otherwise a key from the environment. It's dimmed with no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running. The line under the controls gives the answer:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Checking…" | The check is running. |
| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI took the key in this region. |
| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
| AssemblyAI's own message | The check failed, and the message says why. |

Saving or removing the key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so you don't need to reopen it.

The ⓘ explains what's uploaded, when it's deleted and what AssemblyAI charges. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).

## Playback

This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |

Both save the moment you change them. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Anything you do in Frame Job stops the pass at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.

It never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

## How the key fields behave

The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.

- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".

The line under the controls reports what happened:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |

---
title: "Settings"
description: "Every control in the Settings window: connecting an MCP client, your Anthropic and AssemblyAI keys, the assistant's model, and background rendering."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Settings holds what belongs to you and not to a project: how an MCP client reaches Frame Job, your Anthropic key and the assistant's model, your AssemblyAI key and region, and whether graphics render while you're idle.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Assistant tab ▸ Open Settings…"
/>

<Shot
  name="02-settings.window"
  alt="The Assistant, Transcription and Playback sections of Settings with no keys stored. Assistant has an Anthropic API key field reading Paste your key, a Model field, Compact when context reaches 300,000 tokens ticked, Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens unticked, and Save and Remove buttons. Transcription has an AssemblyAI API key field, Region set to United States, and Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page buttons. Playback has Background render ticked, starting after 5 seconds."
/>

## Opening Settings

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). It works with or without a project open, so you can set your keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It's a window, not a sheet, and it shows the same settings whichever project is open.

The window has four sections, one under the other: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. There are no tabs. On a short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls.

Closing it loses nothing, because every control saves as you use it, or when you press its **Save** button. While it's open it's listed in the **Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.

Two other places send you here:

- With no Anthropic key, the Assistant tab shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button that opens this window.
- With AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note under the button in the Generate Captions sheet, and the button's tooltip, read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The sheet doesn't open Settings for you.

[AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/) says what each key turns on.

## The info buttons

The **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback** headings each carry an ⓘ button that explains the section. The MCP section has none, because its text is shown in full.

- Rest the pointer on it for about a third of a second to see the explanation. Moving away closes it.
- Click it to keep the explanation open. Click it again, click anywhere else, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or close the window to end it.

VoiceOver reads it as "About Assistant", and so on for each section. With keyboard navigation on, <kbd>Space</kbd> presses it.

## MCP

This section tells an MCP client, such as Claude Code, how to reach Frame Job. Clients use `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which connects over a local socket that only programs you run can open. If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background.

Under that text is the full path of the helper inside the copy you're running. You can select and copy it.

**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

The section then says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."

The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job. If the helper is missing from this copy, the button is dimmed and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."

The command is for Claude Code. Other clients use the same helper path in their own configuration. See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

## Assistant

This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic key, the model, and two settings for long conversations. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses, typed as text. Saved when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000, and the field works only while the box is ticked. | On, 300,000 |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn. It never drops tool search results. | Off |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |

There's no **Verify** button here, because Frame Job doesn't call Anthropic itself. Your key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.

**A change to the key or the model starts over.** Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window's Assistant tab, and the next message starts a new one. Pressing <kbd>Return</kbd> in **Model:** without changing the model that's used ends nothing.

**A change to the other two keeps going.** The compaction and clearing settings apply to every open conversation at once and end none of them. They have no **Save** button. A compaction number outside 20,000 to 900,000 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Earlier renders don't survive compaction, and each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).

Under the buttons is what the assistant has cost this month, with a note that the figure is Frame Job's own estimate. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).

The ⓘ sums up what's sent to Anthropic, that it's billed to your key, that the assistant asks before writing a file, where the key is kept, the blank **Model:** default and the two chat settings.

## Transcription

This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** uses them with AssemblyAI chosen, and so does **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Captions made on your Mac need no key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with the key and region, to check they work. | |
| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard in your browser, where you get a key and see what you've spent. | |

A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your AssemblyAI account uses.

**Verify** checks the key a real run would use: one you've typed and not saved, otherwise the stored key, otherwise a key from the environment. It's dimmed with no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running. The line under the controls gives the answer:

| --- | --- |
| "Checking…" | The check is running. |
| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI took the key in this region. |
| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
| AssemblyAI's own message | The check failed, and the message says why. |

Saving or removing the key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so you don't need to reopen it.

The ⓘ explains what's uploaded, when it's deleted and what AssemblyAI charges. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).

## Playback

This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |

Both save the moment you change them. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Anything you do in Frame Job stops the pass at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.

It never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

## How the key fields behave

The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.

- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".

The line under the controls reports what happened:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |

An agent's cloud tools, `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers`, do use the key and region saved here, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop at the point they would send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use is answered without a key. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).

## Related

- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)
