---
title: "What Frame Job remembers"
description: "Which view choices, pane sizes, sheets and panels reopen the way you left them, what starts fresh in each window, and where those choices are kept."
---

Frame Job remembers some of your choices between launches, so the next window or sheet opens the way you left it. These are your choices on this Mac, not part of a project, so none of them travels with a `.framejob` package. The [Settings](/reference/settings/) window has its own page.

## View choices

The last choice you made, in any window, is what the next window opens with. These apply to every project.

| Choice | Where | Options | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Snapping | **View ▸ Snapping**, <kbd>N</kbd>, or **Snap** in the timeline bar | On, off | On |
| Safe area guides | **View ▸ Safe Areas**, or **Safe** in the toolbar | On, off | Off |
| Inspector | **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>), which reads **Show Inspector** while hidden | Shown, hidden | Shown |
| Timeline track height | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸**, or **S**, **M** and **L** in the timeline bar | Small, Medium, Large | Medium |
| Preview quality | **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸** | Full, Half, Quarter | Full |

Preview quality changes only how sharply the preview is drawn while you work. Export and saved frames always render at full size. See [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/).

Holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag turns snapping off for that drag only, and changes nothing that's remembered.

## Pane sizes

Drag the divider above the timeline, or the one left of the inspector, and new windows open at that size.

| Pane | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inspector width | 280 to 440 pt | 304 pt |
| Timeline height | 140 pt to 60% of the window | 300 pt |

The canvas stays at least 380 pt wide, and the area above the timeline at least 220 pt tall.

Only dragging a divider saves a size. Resizing the window, or hiding and showing the inspector, changes nothing that's remembered, and the inspector's width isn't saved while it's hidden.

## Preview Window frame

**View ▸ Preview Window** (<kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd>) opens where the last one was left, on a second display for example. There's one saved frame for every project.

With two projects' previews open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved. Whether the window is open isn't remembered. See [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).

## Sheets

These reopen on what you chose last time. Any sheet not listed here opens on its defaults every time.

| Where | What's remembered | When it's saved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **File ▸ Generate Captions…** | **Engine:** (On this Mac or AssemblyAI), **Style:**, and the **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses** boxes | As you change each one |
| **File ▸ Export…** | The last settings you exported with, except **Dynamic Range** | When you press **Export…** or **Add to Queue** |
| **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** | When you press **Zoom** |
| **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:** | When you press **Follow** |
| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:**, shared with Follow Subject | When you press **Make** |
| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | **Rate:**, **Shortest stretch:** and **Keep pitch** | When you press **Apply** |
| **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** | **Minimum shot:**, **Cut:**, **Crosstalk:** and **Ignore bleed:** | When you press **Switch** |
| The **Normalize** row of the [Volume section](/audio/normalize/) | Its mode, **Peak** or **Loudness**, and its target in LUFS | As you change each one |
| The Document tab's **Canvas** section | **Resize clips proportionally**, used with your next [canvas-size](/projects/canvas-size/) change | As you tick it |

A sheet you cancel saves nothing, where the table says it saves on a press.

The first time you export, the sheet opens on H.264 at document size. Named export presets are kept in a file, so they're on [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).

**Follow:** can read differently in the two sheets that share it. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, it opens on **Speaker** again, and Follow Subject, which has no such choice, opens on **Subject**.

**Resize clips proportionally** is a preference, not an edit, so undo doesn't reach it.

No agent tool reads any of these. An agent's call always names its own values.

## Recorder panel

**File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) reopens on your last choices, each saved as you change it.

| Group | What's remembered |
| --- | --- |
| Source | The display in **Source:**, **Include Frame Job windows** |
| Camera | **Camera:** and **Format:**, **Record the camera too**, **Layout:**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands** |
| Sound | **Microphone:**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **System Audio:** |
| Pointer and keys | **Cursor:**, **Show Clicks:**, **Record shortcuts** |
| When it lands | **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts**, **Speed up typing** |
| Picture | **Rate:**, **Size:** |

Until you change them, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and **Speed up typing** are off, **Zoom in on clicks** and **Show shortcuts** are on, **Layout:** is **Corner**, and **Cursor:** follows the default for the source.

A few things don't last between launches:

- **Record Into:** is never remembered.
- A picked window, **Microphone Only** and **Camera** as the **Source:** row last for the session only. The camera you chose is remembered, even though the row isn't.

See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).

## Inspector sections

Whether each inspector section is collapsed or expanded is remembered, section by section, in every window. Only a click on a section's header is remembered.

A section you've never clicked opens in its default state. Transform, a text or shape's main section, a graphic's Properties, and the sections of the Media and Document tabs start open, and most others start closed. If that would leave a Clip tab with every section shut, the first one you've never closed opens. See [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/).

## Permission questions

macOS shows its Screen Recording prompt only once, so Frame Job remembers that it has already asked. A later press of **Record** without the permission opens the Screen Recording pane of System Settings instead of the prompt. Input Monitoring, which **Record shortcuts** needs, is remembered the same way. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).

## Convert on import

When macOS can't open a file and Frame Job offers to repackage or convert it, ticking **Do this automatically from now on** in that alert remembers your answer:

- Ticked with **Convert** or **Repackage**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails.

There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:

```sh
defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
```

See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

## Update checks

The downloaded copy of Frame Job remembers your answer to whether it should check for updates automatically, and when it last checked. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/).

## What is not remembered

**View ▸ Preview Window**, **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection**, **Show SDR Version**, **Show Subjects**, **Scopes** and **Loudness Meter** all start off in each new window. None of them changes an export.

Nothing about the scopes is kept: a new window starts with Waveform over Vectorscope. The Loudness Meter starts off and empty.

Timeline zoom, Loop, the playhead, the selection and the in/out range aren't remembered between launches.

Some rows in the sheets above are never remembered, even though the rows around them are:

- **Zoom:** in Follow Subject and Make Vertical Version
- **Make a copy** in Make Vertical Version
- **Zoom on typing** in Auto Zoom
- **Record Into:** in the recorder panel
- **Dynamic Range** in Export
- Every choice in **Match Audio…**

## Where these are kept

All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain. So do the model, the region, the compaction and clearing settings, and **Background render** from the Settings window. Your API keys are never stored there.

## Related

- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)
- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)

- **Make a copy** in Make Vertical Version
- **Zoom on typing** in Auto Zoom
- **Record Into:** in the recorder panel
- **Dynamic Range** in Export
- Every choice in **Match Audio…**

## Where these are kept

All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain. So do the model, the region, the compaction and clearing settings, and **Background render** from the Settings window. Your API keys are never stored there.

## Related

- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)
- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)

---
title: "Buttons and context menus"
description: "Every toolbar and timeline-bar button with no menu item, and every right-click menu in Frame Job, with what each item does and when it's greyed."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most commands live in the menu bar, and [Menus](/reference/menus/) lists them. This page covers the rest: the buttons that do something no menu item does, and the menus you open with a right-click.

<AtAGlance
  keys="⌃-click"
  where={['The toolbar', 'The timeline bar', 'Right-click a track, a Media row, an inspector row or a curves channel']}
  tools={['add_shape_clip', 'set_track', 'remove_track', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_action_end', 'set_video', 'record_screen']}
/>

## Buttons with no menu item

Most buttons in the toolbar and the timeline bar repeat a menu item, and their tooltips give its shortcut. These four have no menu item at all.

| Button | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Loop** | Toolbar, at the end of the transport buttons | Turns [looping](/timeline/loop/) on and off. Playback repeats the in/out range when one is set, otherwise the whole timeline. The button is dimmed while Loop is off. |
| **Zoom Out** and **Zoom In** (− and +) | Timeline bar | Zoom the [timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) out or in by a step. |
| **Timeline Zoom** slider | Timeline bar, between − and + | Sets the timeline zoom about the middle of the view. The slider is logarithmic, so the same distance always changes the zoom by the same ratio. |
| **Add Shape** | Timeline bar | Opens the shape menu. See [Add Shape](#add-shape). |

These have their own control, and do the same as a **View** menu item:

| Button | Where | The same as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Fit Timeline** | Timeline bar, after + | **View ▸ Fit Timeline** (<kbd>⇧Z</kbd>) |
| **Snap** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Snapping** (<kbd>N</kbd>) |
| **S**, **M** and **L** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**: Small, Medium and Large tracks |
| Zoom pop-up: **Fit**, **50%**, **100%**, **200%** | Toolbar | The canvas zoom. **View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** move through the same four steps. |
| **Safe** | Toolbar | **View ▸ Safe Areas** |

## Add Shape

The **Add Shape** button in the timeline bar is the only way to add a shape clip. There's no menu bar item for it.

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.
2. Click **Add Shape**.
3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.

</Steps>

The shape goes on the front track at the playhead. If it doesn't fit there, Frame Job adds a new track above everything and puts it on that. The new clip is selected, and the undo step names the shape, for example **Add Ellipse**. See [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/).

## Context menus

Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click opens a menu in four places in the editor:

- [A track's header, or the empty part of its lane](#track-header-or-empty-lane)
- [A row in the Media tab](#media-row)
- [A row in the inspector](#inspector-row)
- [A channel in the Color tab's curves strip](#curves-channel-strip)

A right-click on a clip, the ruler or the timeline's corner opens no menu.

A menu acts on what you clicked, not on the selection or the current track.

### Track header or empty lane

Right-click a track's header, one of the buttons on it, or the empty part of its lane. The menu is for that track, and its checkmarks show that track's own state.

| Item | What it does | Undo step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hide Video** | Turns the track's picture off or on. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). | Hide Track |
| **Mute Audio** | Turns the track's sound off or on. | Mute Track |
| **Lock Track** | Locks or unlocks the track. | Lock Track |
| **Solo** | Solos the track, or stops soloing it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). | Solo Track |
| **Mix…** | Opens the track's mix panel. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). | |
| **Matte ▸** | **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**, with a checkmark on the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/). | Track Matte |
| **Remove Track** | Removes the track. If it holds clips, Frame Job asks first and says how many go with it. Greyed when it's the only track. | Remove Track |

**Remove Track** here is the way to delete an empty track that isn't the front-most one, because an empty track has no clip to select.

### Media row

Right-click a row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). The menu acts on that file, whatever the list's selection is.

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, pushing later clips along, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/). |
| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, replacing what's in the way, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. |
| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips that use the file, scrolls to the first one and switches to the Clip tab. Greyed when no clip on the timeline itself uses the file, which includes a file no clip uses and one used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/). |
| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder: the original, or the project's copy when there's no original. It beeps when it has neither. |
| **Relink…** | Points this entry at a file you choose. It takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate and its audio, video and alpha flags. Frame Job won't relink to a file of another kind, and a clip past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/). |
| **Remove** | Removes the file from the project. An unused file goes at once. A used file asks first, and its clips go with it, including clips inside nests. When the file is a LUT, the clips using it keep their place and lose the look, and any file it converts loses its Camera Log. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |

### Inspector row

Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them. The menu shows only what applies to that row, and with nothing that applies there's no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own menu.

| Item | When it's there | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action. |
| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action. |
| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default. Greyed when it's already there. |
| **Set end value to default** | The row has a default and animates, and an action is selected | Takes the place of **Reset to default**, and sets the row's value at the action's end. Greyed when it's already there. |

On a row the selected action changes, the ◆ in the left gutter turns into × when you hover over it. Click it to remove the row from the action, the same as **Remove from action N**. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

### Curves channel strip

Right-click a cell of the channel strip under the curve editor in the Color tab. **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat** puts that one curve back to flat, and is greyed when it already is.

### Recording status item

This one is in the macOS menu bar, not the editor. While a recording runs its time shows there, and a click opens its menu:

- **Recording keyboard shortcuts**, a dimmed row shown only while shortcuts are being recorded
- **Pause Recording**, or **Resume Recording** while paused
- **Stop Recording**

Its tooltip says whether Frame Job is recording or paused. If you quit while a display or window recording is running with the recorder panel hidden, Frame Job opens this menu so you can stop it.

If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **Pause Recording** still work. See [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/).

## Related

- [Menus](/reference/menus/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
- [Gestures with no menu item](/reference/gestures/)

---
title: "Settings"
description: "Every control in the Settings window: connecting an MCP client, your Anthropic and AssemblyAI keys, the assistant's model, and background rendering."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Settings holds what belongs to you and not to a project: how an MCP client reaches Frame Job, your Anthropic key and the assistant's model, your AssemblyAI key and region, and whether graphics render while you're idle.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Assistant tab ▸ Open Settings…"
/>

<Shot
  name="02-settings.window"
  alt="The Assistant, Transcription and Playback sections of Settings with no keys stored. Assistant has an Anthropic API key field reading Paste your key, a Model field, Compact when context reaches 300,000 tokens ticked, Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens unticked, and Save and Remove buttons. Transcription has an AssemblyAI API key field, Region set to United States, and Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page buttons. Playback has Background render ticked, starting after 5 seconds."
/>

## Opening Settings

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). It works with or without a project open, so you can set your keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It's a window, not a sheet, and it shows the same settings whichever project is open.

The window has four sections, one under the other: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. There are no tabs. On a short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls.

Closing it loses nothing, because every control saves as you use it, or when you press its **Save** button. While it's open it's listed in the **Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.

Two other places send you here:

- With no Anthropic key, the Assistant tab shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button that opens this window.
- With AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note under the button in the Generate Captions sheet, and the button's tooltip, read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The sheet doesn't open Settings for you.

[AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/) says what each key turns on.

## The info buttons

The **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback** headings each carry an ⓘ button that explains the section. The MCP section has none, because its text is shown in full.

- Rest the pointer on it for about a third of a second to see the explanation. Moving away closes it.
- Click it to keep the explanation open. Click it again, click anywhere else, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or close the window to end it.

VoiceOver reads it as "About Assistant", and so on for each section. With keyboard navigation on, <kbd>Space</kbd> presses it.

## MCP

This section tells an MCP client, such as Claude Code, how to reach Frame Job. Clients use `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which connects over a local socket that only programs you run can open. If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background.

Under that text is the full path of the helper inside the copy you're running. You can select and copy it.

**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

The section then says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."

The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job. If the helper is missing from this copy, the button is dimmed and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."

The command is for Claude Code. Other clients use the same helper path in their own configuration. See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

## Assistant

This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic key, the model, and two settings for long conversations. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses, typed as text. Saved when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000, and the field works only while the box is ticked. | On, 300,000 |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn. It never drops tool search results. | Off |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |

There's no **Verify** button here, because Frame Job doesn't call Anthropic itself. Your key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.

**A change to the key or the model starts over.** Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window's Assistant tab, and the next message starts a new one. Pressing <kbd>Return</kbd> in **Model:** without changing the model that's used ends nothing.

**A change to the other two keeps going.** The compaction and clearing settings apply to every open conversation at once and end none of them. They have no **Save** button. A compaction number outside 20,000 to 900,000 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Earlier renders don't survive compaction, and each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).

Under the buttons is what the assistant has cost this month, with a note that the figure is Frame Job's own estimate. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).

The ⓘ sums up what's sent to Anthropic, that it's billed to your key, that the assistant asks before writing a file, where the key is kept, the blank **Model:** default and the two chat settings.

## Transcription

This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** uses them with AssemblyAI chosen, and so does **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Captions made on your Mac need no key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with the key and region, to check they work. | |
| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard in your browser, where you get a key and see what you've spent. | |

A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your AssemblyAI account uses.

**Verify** checks the key a real run would use: one you've typed and not saved, otherwise the stored key, otherwise a key from the environment. It's dimmed with no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running. The line under the controls gives the answer:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Checking…" | The check is running. |
| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI took the key in this region. |
| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
| AssemblyAI's own message | The check failed, and the message says why. |

Saving or removing the key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so you don't need to reopen it.

The ⓘ explains what's uploaded, when it's deleted and what AssemblyAI charges. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).

## Playback

This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |

Both save the moment you change them. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Anything you do in Frame Job stops the pass at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.

It never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

## How the key fields behave

The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.

- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".

The line under the controls reports what happened:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |

[Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) says where the keys are stored, and how a key can come from the environment.

## Agents and Settings

No agent tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Your keys, the model, the region and **Background render** are set only by you, in this window.

An agent's cloud tools, `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers`, do use the key and region saved here, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop at the point they would send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use is answered without a key. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).

## Related

- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)

---
title: "What Frame Job remembers"
description: "Which view choices, pane sizes, sheets and panels reopen the way you left them, what starts fresh in each window, and where those choices are kept."
---

Frame Job remembers some of your choices between launches, so the next window or sheet opens the way you left it. These are your choices on this Mac, not part of a project, so none of them travels with a `.framejob` package. The [Settings](/reference/settings/) window has its own page.

## View choices

The last choice you made, in any window, is what the next window opens with. These apply to every project.

| Choice | Where | Options | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Snapping | **View ▸ Snapping**, <kbd>N</kbd>, or **Snap** in the timeline bar | On, off | On |
| Safe area guides | **View ▸ Safe Areas**, or **Safe** in the toolbar | On, off | Off |
| Inspector | **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>), which reads **Show Inspector** while hidden | Shown, hidden | Shown |
| Timeline track height | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸**, or **S**, **M** and **L** in the timeline bar | Small, Medium, Large | Medium |
| Preview quality | **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸** | Full, Half, Quarter | Full |

Preview quality changes only how sharply the preview is drawn while you work. Export and saved frames always render at full size. See [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/).

Holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag turns snapping off for that drag only, and changes nothing that's remembered.

## Pane sizes

Drag the divider above the timeline, or the one left of the inspector, and new windows open at that size.

| Pane | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inspector width | 280 to 440 pt | 304 pt |
| Timeline height | 140 pt to 60% of the window | 300 pt |

The canvas stays at least 380 pt wide, and the area above the timeline at least 220 pt tall.

Only dragging a divider saves a size. Resizing the window, or hiding and showing the inspector, changes nothing that's remembered, and the inspector's width isn't saved while it's hidden.

## Preview Window frame

**View ▸ Preview Window** (<kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd>) opens where the last one was left, on a second display for example. There's one saved frame for every project.

With two projects' previews open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved. Whether the window is open isn't remembered. See [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).

## Sheets

These reopen on what you chose last time. Any sheet not listed here opens on its defaults every time.

| Where | What's remembered | When it's saved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **File ▸ Generate Captions…** | **Engine:** (On this Mac or AssemblyAI), **Style:**, and the **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses** boxes | As you change each one |
| **File ▸ Export…** | The last settings you exported with, except **Dynamic Range** | When you press **Export…** or **Add to Queue** |
| **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** | When you press **Zoom** |
| **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:** | When you press **Follow** |
| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:**, shared with Follow Subject | When you press **Make** |
| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | **Rate:**, **Shortest stretch:** and **Keep pitch** | When you press **Apply** |
| **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** | **Minimum shot:**, **Cut:**, **Crosstalk:** and **Ignore bleed:** | When you press **Switch** |
| The **Normalize** row of the [Volume section](/audio/normalize/) | Its mode, **Peak** or **Loudness**, and its target in LUFS | As you change each one |
| The Document tab's **Canvas** section | **Resize clips proportionally**, used with your next [canvas-size](/projects/canvas-size/) change | As you tick it |

A sheet you cancel saves nothing, where the table says it saves on a press.

The first time you export, the sheet opens on H.264 at document size. Named export presets are kept in a file, so they're on [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).

**Follow:** can read differently in the two sheets that share it. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, it opens on **Speaker** again, and Follow Subject, which has no such choice, opens on **Subject**.

**Resize clips proportionally** is a preference, not an edit, so undo doesn't reach it.

No agent tool reads any of these. An agent's call always names its own values.

## Recorder panel

**File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) reopens on your last choices, each saved as you change it.

| Group | What's remembered |
| --- | --- |
| Source | The display in **Source:**, **Include Frame Job windows** |
| Camera | **Camera:** and **Format:**, **Record the camera too**, **Layout:**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands** |
| Sound | **Microphone:**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **System Audio:** |
| Pointer and keys | **Cursor:**, **Show Clicks:**, **Record shortcuts** |
| When it lands | **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts**, **Speed up typing** |
| Picture | **Rate:**, **Size:** |

Until you change them, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and **Speed up typing** are off, **Zoom in on clicks** and **Show shortcuts** are on, **Layout:** is **Corner**, and **Cursor:** follows the default for the source.

A few things don't last between launches:

- **Record Into:** is never remembered.
- A picked window, **Microphone Only** and **Camera** as the **Source:** row last for the session only. The camera you chose is remembered, even though the row isn't.

See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).

## Inspector sections

Whether each inspector section is collapsed or expanded is remembered, section by section, in every window. Only a click on a section's header is remembered.

A section you've never clicked opens in its default state. Transform, a text or shape's main section, a graphic's Properties, and the sections of the Media and Document tabs start open, and most others start closed. If that would leave a Clip tab with every section shut, the first one you've never closed opens. See [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/).

## Permission questions

macOS shows its Screen Recording prompt only once, so Frame Job remembers that it has already asked. A later press of **Record** without the permission opens the Screen Recording pane of System Settings instead of the prompt. Input Monitoring, which **Record shortcuts** needs, is remembered the same way. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).

## Convert on import

When macOS can't open a file and Frame Job offers to repackage or convert it, ticking **Do this automatically from now on** in that alert remembers your answer:

- Ticked with **Convert** or **Repackage**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails.

There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:

```sh
defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
```

See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

## Update checks

The downloaded copy of Frame Job remembers your answer to whether it should check for updates automatically, and when it last checked. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/).

## What is not remembered

**View ▸ Preview Window**, **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection**, **Show SDR Version**, **Show Subjects**, **Scopes** and **Loudness Meter** all start off in each new window. None of them changes an export.

Nothing about the scopes is kept: a new window starts with Waveform over Vectorscope. The Loudness Meter starts off and empty.

Timeline zoom, Loop, the playhead, the selection and the in/out range aren't remembered between launches.

Some rows in the sheets above are never remembered, even though the rows around them are:

- **Zoom:** in Follow Subject and Make Vertical Version
- **Make a copy** in Make Vertical Version
- **Zoom on typing** in Auto Zoom
- **Record Into:** in the recorder panel
- **Dynamic Range** in Export
- Every choice in **Match Audio…**

## Where these are kept

All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain. So do the model, the region, the compaction and clearing settings, and **Background render** from the Settings window. Your API keys are never stored there.

## Related

- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)
- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and
  `VideoPatch.cutout`; its `dictionary` writes all five keys), `CutoutPatch` (the sparse
  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
